chunks: I say what you are hearing.
And Allah is the One sought for help against myself and yourselves.
And He is sufficient for us,
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Wa ni'mal wakeel' mean in the context of seeking Allah's help?
ai.summary: In this opening formula, Imam Ali (AS) establishes rhetorical humility by attributing the speech to human effort while relying on divine support, a practice reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between human agency and God's will. By citing 'Wa Ni'mal Wakeel', he underscores the theological principle of Tawakkul, reminding the audience that despite the eloquence of the sermon, ultimate sufficiency lies in Allah. This brief invocation sets a spiritual tone for the discourse on the Quran, linking the act of listening to the divine trustworthiness that sustains the revelation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: I say what you are hearing.
I seek Allāh’s help for myself and yourselves.
and He is an excellent trustee [3:173].
